findings.message: The Category chip options use the lowercase values `dev`/`uat`/`prod`. The draft keeps whatever case the model sends: the tool description says "Dev, UAT or Prod", and the scripted rule sends `category: "UAT"`. `initialValues` copies `input.category` as is. FormChips then matches options with `o.value === value`, so no chip shows as picked, but the hidden "UAT" is still submitted and passes `CategoryInput`. The card hides a value it is about to write. Fix: parse the draft's category with `CategoryInput` (lowercase it) in `ReleaseDraft`, or normalise it before the form values are built. Add a test with Dev, UAT and Prod in mixed case.
findings.scenario: "Create release v2.6.0 of CON: Portal refresh, UAT, 2026-12-01 to 2026-12-12" → the card shows no Category chip picked → the person confirms → the release is created with category uat, which the card never showed as chosen.

findings.message: `proposeRelease` writes its own copy of the field rules instead of using the service's schema pieces. The name check is a hand-written `!a.name.trim()` with no `.max(120)` from `ReleaseName`. The date message is a new string instead of `Day`'s errors. An empty version is skipped where the service has `version.min(1)`. The per-field check and the confirm can disagree. Fix: validate each present field with `ReleaseName`, `Day`, `CategoryInput` and the service's version schema (`safeParse`, using their messages), so there is one rule.
findings.scenario: Name = 130 characters → the per-field check passes and the card shows no error → Create is refused by the service with a generic input error, not on the Name field.

findings.message: `inApp` rejects only `//` and `/\` straight after the leading slash. Browsers strip tab, CR and LF from URLs, so `/\t/evil.example` passes this check and becomes `//evil.example`, a different host. The test says "never another host" but covers only two spellings. Fix: reject any control character or whitespace too (e.g. `/^\/(?![/\\])[^\s\x00-\x1f]*$/`), or resolve with `new URL(url, base)` and compare the origin. Add those variants to the test.
findings.scenario: openOf({ open: { label: 'x', url: '/\t/evil.example' } }) → accepted as in-app, no ↗ → clicking it goes to evil.example.

findings.message: Formatting: `ReleaseName =z.string()` is missing the space after `=`. `release-tracking.ts` also has a stray blank line where `releaseState` was removed.

`openElsewhere` only counts another release as holding a proposal while that release is not completed. So a Verified proposal that sits in a completed release is listed on the card with no detail and no "Move from their release" box. Both writers then quietly take it out of that completed release, with no `reassign` needed. 123 says a completed release can't change (it refuses `set_release_proposals` and `tag_release`), yet this changes what the completed release contains. Fix: treat membership of a completed release as `shippedElsewhere`, or at least require `reassign` for it too, the same as for an open release. Show the same detail on the card.
findings.scenario: v1 (category Dev) holds CON-020, which is Verified. A Dev deployment completes v1. Creating v2 with proposalKeys=[CON-020] and no reassign succeeds: CON-020 leaves the completed v1, and the card never warned about it.

findings.message: `valueOf` drops ticked keys that are not among the shown options. A proposal key that the model or user put in the draft and that isn't eligible (Building, withdrawn, shipped, or a typo) disappears on confirm and is never refused. The person sees an unticked list and a release created without that proposal. Fix: in `proposeRelease`, check the draft's `proposalKeys` against the eligible list for the starting input so the refusal shows on the field, or keep unknown keys so the service refuses them.
findings.scenario: "Create release v2.6.0 of CON with CON-014" (CON-014 is Building): the draft has proposalKeys=CON-014, the card shows nothing ticked, and confirming creates the release with 0 proposals and no message.

findings.message: The "latest release" query (order by created_at desc limit 1) is a second copy of the one in pin-offers.ts:36. Today they agree, so the pin offer's version matches the card's filled-in version. If one copy changes, the prompt "Create release vX" and the card's Version field will disagree. Fix: share one query helper.
